prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: preview-only Chinese faction lettering study for a Three Kingdoms card game.
Primary request: a matching set of three original artistic Chinese characters, exactly 魏, 蜀, 吴.
Scene/backdrop: flat warm ivory backdrop with generous clean margins.
Composition: three isolated, equally prominent glyphs arranged in one horizontal row: 魏 on the left, 蜀 in the center, 吴 on the right. Each occupies its own equal-width cell, no visible grid. All three entirely in frame, no overlapping strokes.
Style/medium: 金石篆刻, carved-stone seal-cutting inspired lettering, powerful squared strokes, compact well-balanced silhouettes, slight hand-cut edge irregularities, very restrained stone abrasion. Dark cinnabar red strokes. Modern readable Chinese forms with seal-cutting character, NOT illegible archaic script. Not a standard computer font.
Text (verbatim): 魏 蜀 吴. Render each exactly once. 魏 must retain 禾 and 女 on the left and 鬼 on the right; 蜀 must remain recognizable; 吴 must be the simplified form with 口 above 天, not 吳.
Constraints: only these three glyphs, no other writing, numbers, labels, frames, seals around the glyphs, calligrapher signatures, watermarks, animals, weapons, scenery or flags. Thick clean primary strokes and readable negative spaces suitable for a small faction badge. Material texture should not break the strokes. This is a style comparison sheet, not a full game UI.
